region: Ovid · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Six Eighty Cellars sits on the steep west shore of Cayuga Lake, near Ovid. Dave and Melissa Pittard of Skaneateles, who also own nearby Buttonwood Grove Winery, bought the former Toro Run Winery in 2020 for its established vineyards, and opened Six Eighty in 2021. The name comes from the land itself: the slope rises 680 feet from the bottom of the lake to the top of the property. Head winemaker Ian Barry works with certified-sustainable estate fruit and a low-intervention approach.

The cellar is unusual for the region: instead of oak barrels or steel tanks, wines are raised in clay, terracotta, stone and concrete vessels, and the winery leans toward less common grapes such as Grüner Veltliner, Austria’s signature white, and toward pét-nats made in the méthode ancestrale. For this one, estate Grüner Veltliner is harvested in October, pressed and settled, and left to begin fermenting on its own yeasts; the wine is bottled before fermentation finishes, so the last of the sugar creates a gentle natural sparkle in the bottle.

Pét-nats are usually bottled with their fine yeast sediment still in, so a little haze is part of the style, and a gentle pour keeps the sediment settled for anyone who prefers it clear. The winery describes pear, tart apple and lemon on the nose, leading to a chalky, savoury minerality on a crisp, dry palate. Six Eighty also makes pét-nats from Pinot Meunier rosé and Merlot, alongside still wines raised in its earthenware vessels.
